ops.title: Wire ccp doctor/status to Manager.StrandedCredentialRecoveries()
ops.description:
Follow-up to review finding F1 (commits 4b3eadf + 648d508). Deliberately NOT
done on the v0.21 migration branch: it is new surface, not a defect fix, and
that branch already carried seven fixes to lifecycle-critical code.

The seam exists and is tested. `Manager.StrandedCredentialRecoveries()` returns
(AccountID, Token, Cause), sorted, mutex-guarded, with regression coverage
asserting it lists a fenced account while stranded and empties after recovery.
What remains is one call plus rendering in the daemon/cli lane.

Why it matters: as shipped, a fenced account is only observable to a caller who
attempts an operation against it and receives ErrCredentialRecoveryPending. An
account nobody touches stays silently fenced until the daemon restarts —
harmless for that account, but an operator has no way to see that recovery
partially failed. The log line alone is not enough; a log line is exactly what
made the original F1 strand invisible.

Scope is small: read the accessor, render account + cause. No new state, no
polling contract — the map is in-memory and generation-scoped by design (a
crash mints a new owner and the re-scan re-presents the row).

ops.text: ccp doctor (or the status surface) reports fenced accounts with account, token, and cause
A fenced account is visible to an operator without having to attempt an operation against it
